doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Mugsy's career: studying music, Ted Lewis, Pollack
summary: Mugsy learned to read after two years, spent eight years with Ted Lewis and then joined Ben Pollack.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: When you were first started, were you studying music? Or who did you start thinking? No, I started out thinking first, then I started to study. Later? Oh, yeah. After I was playing professionally about two years, then I started to study. Because you couldn't play in bands. You couldn't go to a pit or anything with that if you couldn't read. Well, from Ray Miller, yeah, I went to Ted Lewis. That was a nice sentence. Eight years hardly. How many years? Eight years. Eight years. I don't know what a depression was. I was making $250 a week during the depression. Is that so? I took care of my whole family and I raised a family. Sure. That was good. I was making $250 a week during the Depression. Is that so? I took care of my whole family and I raised a family. Sure. That was good. That's great. After Ted Lewis I couldn't stand it any longer. I went with Benny Pollack. Benny Pollack wound up in the hospital. You know the doctor that operated me, Ockman Ochsner? He was just sitting around the finest surgeons in the world. Yes, he's a famous. Who's that? Ockman Ochsner. At Turo. No, he said he had his own Ockman Ochsner, a foundation hospital. Oh yeah? New hospital. One of the most modern equipment hospitals in the world.

What hospital did you go to New Orleans, to Turo? That's where you are. You remember Turo Infirmary? Yeah. That's where every night when you called your number I said Turo Infirmary. But I didn't know that was the hospital you see here. See, I didn't know you knew what I was talking about. I said sure. Are you calling you all wrong?

There's no answer. Well, Archie was president of the Cancer Society. Just name it. He was the head of it. He was a fabulous man. Wonderful man too. We've been friends ever since the operations. Where are you now? 39.
